questions.problem: Find the fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of ${cos}^{2}⁡(x)$ about $x=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=a$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a)+\frac{{f}^{″}(a)}{2!}(x-a)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(a)}{3!}(x-a)^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(a)}{4!}(x-a)^{4}.
$$

Here, we have $a=\pi ,$ so

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=f(\pi )+{f}^{′}(\pi )(x-\pi )+\frac{{f}^{″}(\pi )}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(\pi )}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\pi )}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.
$$

So we need to work out $f(\pi ),$ ${f}^{′}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{″}(\pi ),$ ${f}^{‴}(\pi )$ and ${f}^{(4)}(\pi ),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(x) & ⟹ &  & f(\pi ) & ={cos}^{2}⁡(\pi )=1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\pi ) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\pi ) & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=-2 \\ {f}^{‴}(x) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{‴}(\pi ) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )=0 \\ {f}^{(4)}(x) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⟹ &  & {f}^{(4)}(\pi ) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${P}_{4}(x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{4}(x) & =1+(0)(x-\pi )+\frac{(-2)}{2!}{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{0}{3!}{(x-\pi )}^{3}+\frac{8}{4!}{(x-\pi )}^{4} \\  & =1-{(x-\pi )}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{(x-\pi )}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Obtaining a Higher-Order Derivative Of a Function Given its Higher-Degree Taylor Polynomial
questions.problem:
The fifth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is given by

$$
{P}_{5}(x)=1-\frac{1}{2}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{3}+\frac{1}{24}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}-\frac{1}{96}{(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{5}.
$$

What is ${f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})?$
questions.worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${(x-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{4}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{4!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{4!} & =\frac{1}{24} \\ \frac{{f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{24} & =\frac{1}{24} \\ {f}^{(4)}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=1+3x+\frac{9}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{27}{8}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{‴}(0)?$

questions.worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{‴}(0)}{3!}.$ Therefore,

$$

$$
